name: Moss-Requiem
description: Moss-Requiem is a world in the long process of dying. Its once-lush surface has contracted to scattered patches of hardy moss and lichen clinging to the margins of dried ocean basins, surrounded by vast plains of petrified forest stumps that stretch to every horizon. A massive impact crater in the northern hemisphere, over three hundred kilometers across, marks the event that set this decline in motion. The sky is a washed-out blue, thin and pale, as though the atmosphere itself is fading.

There is a profound stillness to Moss-Requiem that borders on the sacred. Wind moves across the petrified plains with a hollow whistling, and the moss fields absorb sound so completely that standing among them feels like being wrapped in silence. The temperature rarely rises above comfortable, lending the world a perpetual quality of cool autumn afternoon, beautiful and melancholic in equal measure.

A failed terraforming initiative left rusting atmospheric processors scattered across the equatorial zone, their half-completed work having slowed but not reversed the biosphere's collapse. An abandoned mining complex in the crater basin suggests that economic interests moved on once the easy extractions were complete, leaving Moss-Requiem to its slow fade. The moss species that survive are found nowhere else in cataloged space, having adapted to conditions that exist only here.

Xenobotanists have declared Moss-Requiem a conservation priority, but funding remains scarce for a world with no strategic value. The remaining moss fields are shrinking by measurable percentages each decade, and with them goes a unique biochemistry that may hold keys to atmospheric regeneration on other failing worlds. It is a race against entropy, and entropy is winning.
